docs.title: dengueriskcdmx
docs.text: Data and rasters supporting the Risk Map of Dengue Transmission in the Metropolitan Area of Mexico City. This is the Python version of the R package dengueriskcdmx; it ships the same data sets and rasters.

docs.title: Installation
docs.text:
pip install dengueriskcdmx            # data loaders (GeoPandas)
pip install "dengueriskcdmx[raster]"  # plus rasterio, to read the rasters

docs.title: What is included
docs.text:
Function Returns load_ae_aegypti("all") Ae. aegypti ovitrap presences and pseudo-absences, 2017-2024, with the split column (train / test) load_ae_aegypti("train") / ("test") Training (80%) and test (20%) partitions load_ae_aegypti("external") External validation data, 2025 load_aoi() Study area (Mexico City Metropolitan Area) ae_raster_path(layer) / read_raster(layer) Path to / open GeoTIFF of "aedes", "dengue" or "risk"

Data availability

The ovitrap data are included. The data on confirmed dengue cases used to fit the case model are not published; only the derived probability and risk rasters are provided.

docs.title: Data
docs.text:
Layer Content "aedes" Probability of Ae. aegypti occurrence "dengue" Probability of confirmed imported dengue cases "risk" Two bands: cluster (k-means) and risk (five-level epidemiological risk)

The rasters (about 500 m) are derived from the consensus (mean of the probabilities) of Random Forest, LightGBM and XGBoost models.

docs.title: Quick Start
docs.text:
import dengueriskcdmx as dr

x = dr.load_ae_aegypti("train")
print(x["class"].value_counts())

with dr.read_raster("risk") as r:
    risk = r.read(2)

Each data set has the class (presence / pseudoabs), nine predictors (built, tree, ndvi, prcp, ia, ice, im, pop, hfp) and the point geometry (EPSG:4326). The partition is 80/20, stratified by class, with seed 12345.
